items.title: Treasury could force Revolut and Monzo to fund high street banking
items.summary: The government could make digital banks like Revolut and Monzo pay for shared high street banking facilities after a government review “left the door open” to potentially forcing app-only lenders to pitch in. The Treasury is expected to lay legislation in 2028 that will create a new obligation for major banking providers to protect in-person [...]
items.body:
Treasury could force Revolut and Monzo to fund high street banking
The government could make digital banks like Revolut and Monzo pay for shared high street banking facilities after a government review “left the door open” to potentially forcing app-only lenders to pitch in.
The Treasury is expected to lay legislation in 2028 that will create a new obligation for major banking providers to protect in-person services.
It follows a review from former Which? director Richard Lloyd after the shuttering of nearly 7,000 branches since 2015. Lloyd recommended a new legal requirement for banks to fill service gaps in a move that is expected to lead to the opening of more shared hubs.
But it is yet to be clear which providers will be responsible for funding the shared sites after the review suggested digital banks could fall within the scope.
“Large numbers of customers of digital-only banks frequently rely on physical cash services,” the review said.
Under the current regime, the Treasury decides which banks are legally “designated,” and therefore made to fund cash access fixes like banking hubs, based on their share of the current account market.
But the review has floated switching the designation test to “share of transactions,” which would capture the likes of Revolut, Monzo and Starling, which process high volumes of everyday payments and card transactions.
“The fault line is with the digital banks… the review leaves the door open to [their inclusion in funding],” one industry source familiar with the matter said.
They added it was “exactly in the Treasury’s gift” to decide on the funding framework.
Treasury and banks set for standoff
City minister Lucy Rigby said it was “vital” that the new framework was “agile and adaptable so that it can respond to our changing world”.
Lloyd said in the review it was “entirely feasible” for action in 2027 ahead of the legislation being laid.
But sources close to the discussions said there could be a period of gridlock with larger banks holding back on delivering more hubs until the funding argument is settled.
“It probably limits the full extent of what can actually be done in 2027,” one source said.
Another industry source said it “feels like the can has been kicked down the road” on key decisions around the framework.
Trade body UK Finance, which represents traditional banks and some fintechs, said: “The framework should build on what already works and remain flexible as customer needs change over time.”
Revolut, Monzo and the Treasury did not respond to requests for comment.

items.title: Milburn Review recommendations welcomed by convenience leaders
items.summary: Proposals to cut the cost of employing those under 25 have been welcomed by the Association of Convenience Stores (ACS). One of the big proposals in the Milburn Review is to reduce employer national insurance contributions for younger staff. The review, “From a Welfare State… This story continues at Milburn Review recommendations welcomed by convenience leaders Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
One of the big proposals in the Milburn Review is to reduce employer national insurance contributions for younger staff.
The review, “From a Welfare State to a Working State”, aims to tackle the growing number of young people not in education, employment or training (NEETs).
Recommendations in the review include:
- Government should not increase the costs to employers of hiring young people still further. It should publish a youth employment cost index every two years itemising the financial impact of its decisions on the youth labour market.
- On the minimum wage, the government should continue to direct the Low Pay Commission to judge the pace of convergence between the young person’s rate and the adult rate against the critical goal of protecting youth employment.
- For young retail and hospitality workers, doubling the point at which employer National Insurance becomes payable for those young people, from the current £5,000 threshold to £10,000 in the next five years.
- Employers who take on any young person who has not been in education, employment or training for six months should receive a £3,000 payment. This would extend eligibility to the 314,000 NEETs who are hidden and not in the benefit system at all.
- An extra premium payment of £2,000 should go to employers taking on somebody facing substantially greater barriers, such as care-leavers or disabled young people.
The ACS and others have already raised concerns about the effect of changes to employer national insurance contributions, which made it more expensive to hire people when the government lowered the employer NICs threshold from £9,100 to £5,000 in 2025.
Retailers have reported that rising employment costs have led to fewer staff hours in the business, retailers taking on more hours themselves, and investment decisions being delayed or cancelled to make ends meet.
ACS chief executive Ed Woodall said: “Proposals to reduce employer national insurance costs when taking on young people will be welcomed by convenience retailers.
“Local shops provide secure, local, flexible jobs, but rising employment costs have made it difficult for retailers to take on new starters and offer more hours.
“If the government wants to increase opportunities for young people, it must also make it easier and more affordable for businesses to create those jobs.”
Other leaders in retailing also welcomed the review and encouraged the government to go even further.
Ross Shuttleworth, delivery director for retail at apprenticeship provider Lifetime Training, said: “Retail has long provided young people with an important first step into work.
“The ambition to significantly increase apprenticeship participation and completions is welcome, but delivering it will require employers to have the confidence to create opportunities and clear progression routes for people once they are in work.
“The report is right to consider reducing employer national insurance costs for 21- to 24-year-olds in retail and hospitality.
“It is also right that financial incentives should reward retention rather than simply recruitment. The aim cannot just be to get more young people through the door. It has to be to help them stay and succeed.
“But retention shouldn’t be the end of the ambition either. Young people need somewhere to progress.”
Sarah Bradbury, chief executive at the IGD industry think-tank, said: “IGD welcomes the Milburn review, in particular its focus on early intervention in connecting young people with opportunities in work, education and training.
“Reducing NEET numbers requires coordinated action and, as one of the UK’s largest employers, the food and drink industry has a major role to play.”

items.title: Ikea boss slams Budget as 'missed opportunity' as it abandons new UK store openings due to rising costs
items.summary: David McCabe, who oversees UK and Ireland, criticised the Government for not doing enough to help firms with 'the structural challenges holding the sector back'.
items.body:
Ikea boss slams Budget as 'missed opportunity' as it abandons new UK store openings due to rising costs
Ikea has dubbed the Budget a ‘missed opportunity’ to help beleaguered retailers as it abandons some new store openings in the UK due to rising taxes and costs.
David McCabe, who oversees the Swedish retailer’s operations in the UK and Ireland, criticised the Government for not doing enough to help firms with ‘the structural challenges holding the sector back’.
And pointing to the rising burden of business rates, he said some investment plans have been ditched.
‘Companies like Ikea are looking at incredibly high costs and an increasingly complex operating environment,’ said McCabe.
‘We believe the UK is definitely a market for investment and have recently invested in eight new units in the UK.
‘But there are higher costs and complexities here, and it has meant that we have had investment projects in the UK that we have had to abandon, and that is a shame.’
Ikea has become the latest well-known retailer to bemoan the Budget as a 'missed opportunity'
He joins the growing chorus of household names that have criticised John Healey's first Budget. The British Retail Consortium, which represents the likes of Tesco and Next, described it as 'smoke and mirrors'.
The Government promised to help High Street retailers with their business rates bills - but many still face a 3.5 per cent increase next April.
Ikea’s shops in the UK face the ‘highest rates burden of any Ikea market in Europe’ and the third highest across the world, McCabe said.
These costs are making it harder to stop prices rising for customers, he said.
His remarks follow those of Marks & Spencer chief executive Stuart Machin, who described the Chancellor 's Budget as ‘a whole lot of nothing’.
Businesses were relieved that the sector did not get hammered with additional costs, as they had been in Labour’s first Budget when they were hit with dramatic rises to employer National Insurance contributions.
But Ikea has said that it has decided to put plans for new stores on ice due to the high costs associated with operating physical retail in the UK.
McCabe added: ‘While the Budget avoided adding further costs, it missed an opportunity to back retailers under real pressure, stopping short of addressing the structural challenges holding the sector back.
‘Retail is a vital part of the UK economy and communities nationwide and a more competitive operating environment would help businesses invest with confidence, while continuing to keep prices as low as possible for customers.’
It came as the business, which has 31 stores in the UK, said its retail sales in the country rose just 0.5 per cent to £2.26billion for the year to the end of August.
It blamed ‘a challenging trading environment with weakened consumer confidence and sustained pressure on household budgets’ for hitting revenues in the second half of the year.
As households opt against moving house due to economic pressures, the business said it would focus on sales of storage and organisation products in the current year.
It said that ‘many households are choosing to make their existing spaces work harder rather than moving home.’

items.title: TG Jones put up for sale by private equity owners who rebranded it from WH Smith in fresh blow for High Street
items.summary: TG Jones, which traded under the WH Smith name for over 200 years, is being put up for sale by its private equity owners just weeks before Christmas.
items.body:
TG Jones put up for sale by private equity owners who rebranded it from WH Smith in fresh blow for High Street
TG Jones, which traded under the WH Smith name for over 200 years, is being put up for sale by its private equity owners just weeks before Christmas.
Modella Capital, which bought WH Smith's high street arm and rebranded it as TG Jones last year, has called in advisors to oversee the process.
TG Jones becomes the second British retailer set to change hands after a controversial spell under private equity ownership.
Poundland is battling for survival after its US owners Gordon Brothers, which bought the retailer for £1 last year, rejected a rescue bid.
Politicians and retail veterans have warned that Poundland's demise exposes a worrying trend that has seen private equity vultures prey on household names across Britain.
TG Jones is the rebranded name for the WH Smith High Street shops bought by Modella Capital for £40m last year and is reportedly now being put up for a sale
Founded just four years ago, Modella Capital has gained a reputation for buying distressed British retailers and shutting shops, including at Claire's Accessories and The Original Factory Shop.
Modella bought the TG Jones business for £40million last year and has faced sharp criticism over its running of the business as it plans a swathe of store closures.
In the summer, it revealed plans to shut up to 150 of its remaining 450 shops as part of a restructuring programme, adding to the dismay among customers and workers about the fate of what was once one of the best-known British brands.
It is understood that any transaction would not take place until at least the first quarter of 2027, as first reported by Sky News.
TG Jones and Modella Capital told Sky News: 'High-street retailer TGJones has received unsolicited offers for the business; management and owner Modella Capital have jointly agreed to instruct Teneo Corporate Finance to review these offers and undertake a market-testing exercise.'
Falling sales before Modella's restructuring plan have reportedly narrowed from double digits earlier this year to low single digits.
The WH Smith name vanished from High Streets and is now only used for the business that still owns airport and station stories
TG Jones boss Alex Willson said: 'As ever, our focus is on providing a great experience for customers, especially with the critical Christmas period coming up.
'We continue to execute our turnaround plan, which is improving our performance month by month.
'We're grateful to our fantastic colleagues for their commitment; and to our suppliers, our owner and other stakeholders for their continued support.'
The sale of TG Jones will reportedly not involve considerations around financial engineering, as with Poundland.
Poundland, which filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the high court last month, closed around 200 shops as part of a sweeping restructuring under the US investment house.
Gordon Brothers put the retailer up for sale in September despite a rebound in sales. It has since rejected a bid that would have saved the whole company and its 600 stores, before securing a two-week reprieve to secure a rescue deal.
The discount retailer's owners have tried to ensure that any solvent buyer of the chain repays its £22.5million of a £30million shareholder loan it acquired for £1.
It has prompted Gordon Brothers to reject a number of solvent offers, prompting fury from policymakers.
Lord Sikka said the Government must 'investigate private equity business model', which has 'devoured' town centres and jobs.
Liam Byrne MP, chair of the business committee, has called for 'wholesale accounting reform to ensure that there is real transparency, and potentially, proper stress tests' before investors are 'allowed to overload a business with debt'.

items.title: Car park machine at my local retail park wasn't working, but I STILL got a £100 fine: DEAN DUNHAM reveals exactly how to challenge an 'unfair' parking penalty
items.summary: I tried to pay £1.80 to park at a retail park, but the coin slot was jammed. I have received a parking charge notice for £100 or £60 if paid within 14 days. Is this fair? What can I do?
items.body:
Car park machine at my local retail park wasn't working, but I STILL got a £100 fine: DEAN DUNHAM reveals exactly how to challenge an 'unfair' parking penalty
Updated:
I tried to pay £1.80 to park at a retail park, but the coin slot was jammed. I attempted to pay by credit card, but wasn't sure if the payment went through as it didn’t print a receipt. I felt I had done what I could to try to pay but it seems I failed through no fault of my own. I then carried on with my shopping. I have received a parking charge notice for £100 or £60 if paid within 14 days. Is this fair? What can I do?
R.W. by email.
Dean Dunham replies: You have a good argument for challenging this charge, and I would certainly appeal before considering payment. First, this is a private parking charge, not a fine in the criminal sense. It is essentially a claim that you breached the contractual terms governing the car park.
There is also an important development in your favour. The Government’s new Private Parking Code of Practice, which was laid before Parliament last month, specifically addresses faulty payment machines.
It requires parking operators to explain clearly what motorists should do when payment equipment is unavailable, including whether alternative payment methods are available and whether motorists must leave if they cannot pay.
Crucially, the code’s Appeals Charter says that a parking charge should be cancelled where payment machines are out of operation and no reasonable alternative payment method is available. That is potentially very significant in your case.
The Government’s new Private Parking Code of Practice, which was laid before Parliament last month, specifically addresses faulty payment machines
You had made reasonable efforts to pay, and you should not be penalised if the operator’s equipment prevented you from doing so and no reasonable alternative was available. First, check your credit card statement to establish whether the £1.80 was debited. Write to the parking operator.
Explain what happened, provide any evidence and ask them to investigate the machine’s payment records and maintenance logs. Also ask them to identify what alternative payment arrangements were available and what their signage instructed motorists to do when machines failed.
If the operator rejects your appeal, you can take it to the independent appeals service: POPLA if the operator belongs to the BPA, or the IAS if it belongs to the IPC. I would also draw the operator’s attention expressly to clauses 6.1 and 19 of the new Government code of practice.
Before the new Code, there was no hard-and-fast rule that a broken or jammed machine automatically wiped out the charge.
The onus sat with the driver to take reasonable steps and prove it, retry the machine, look for another, try paying by phone or online, or contact the operator using the number on the signage.
A challenge then rested on general contract fairness and the operator’s trade-association code, rather than any rule obliging them to cancel. By contrast, we now have an automatic right for the ticket to be cancelled in these circumstances.
The new rules are not retrospective, so anyone who received a parking charge before they were in place is still governed by the old system.
Share this article
HOW THIS IS MONEY CAN HELP
Screeching London Underground trains on my commute are so loud it gives me headaches and I fear it’s damaging my hearing. Do I have any rights?
Name and address supplied
Dean Dunham replies: The noise on parts of the Underground can be genuinely punishing, and there is published evidence that some passengers are exposed to very high noise levels. A study published in 2020 found that noise levels on the Underground regularly exceeded 80 decibels, with some readings above 100 decibels. However, it is important to distinguish between noise that is unpleasant and noise that is likely to cause hearing damage. The length and frequency of exposure are important factors.
As a passenger, you do not have the same protections as a Tube employee under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005.
But that does not mean Transport for London (TfL) has no responsibilities. It must operate its services with reasonable care, and if excessive noise caused an identifiable injury because TfL had failed to take reasonable steps to address a foreseeable risk, there could potentially be grounds for a negligence claim. However, proving that would require medical and other supporting evidence. A headache or concern about possible future hearing damage would not, on its own, establish a claim.
First, if you are experiencing headaches or changes in your hearing, seek medical advice and consider having a hearing test.
Second, make a formal complaint to TfL. Identify the exact line and sections of track where the screeching occurs, and ask what noise measurements TfL has taken and what steps it is taking to reduce the problem. TfL has acknowledged that certain sections of track are noisy and can cause discomfort to passengers.
Third, consider using suitable noise-reducing earplugs on particularly noisy journeys, while ensuring you can still hear important announcements and remain aware of your surroundings.

Pret a Manger and KFC press Healey to accept Milburn Neet measures
items.summary: The bosses of high street businesses including Young’s, Pret A Manger and KFC have urged John Healey to slash employer’s national insurance following Alan Milburn’s review into the UK’s Neet crisis. The retail and hospitality sectors have long argued that mounting taxes and red tape have made hiring young people prohibitively difficult and expensive. Milburn’s [...]
items.body:
Pret a Manger and KFC press Healey to accept Milburn Neet measures
The bosses of high street businesses including Young’s, Pret A Manger and KFC have urged John Healey to slash employer’s national insurance following Alan Milburn’s review into the UK’s Neet crisis.
The retail and hospitality sectors have long argued that mounting taxes and red tape have made hiring young people prohibitively difficult and expensive. Milburn’s long-awaited report highlighted the impact of Labour tax hikes on employment costs.
The former health secretary said on Tuesday that Labour’s hikes to employer national insurance contributions (NICs) and its upcoming crackdown on flexible working have made it harder for high street bosses to hire young workers.
The number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet), which is nearing one million, is costing the UK economy billions every year, Milburn warned. Lower youth worklessness could boost the country’s GDP by 0.4 per cent each year, he found.
At the 2024 Budget, then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves hiked the rate of employer NICs to 15 per cent and nearly halved the threshold at which employers start paying it. The £25.7bn raised each year by this tax comes “directly from the bottom line of businesses,” Milburn said.
He told the government it should begin to unwind Reeves’ hikes to NICs by doubling the threshold at which retail and hospitality firms must pay for workers aged between 21 and 24, from £5,000 to £10,000.
NICs cut ‘exactly what pubs need’
The pub sector, which is one of the biggest employers of young people, has urged the Chancellor to adopt this measure. Simon Dodd, chief executive of Young’s, said he would “welcome any proposal that makes it easier for businesses to give young people their first step into work”.
Andy Spencer, chief executive of Punch Pubs, said Milburn’s call for a NICs cut is “exactly the kind of bold, practical intervention we need if we are serious about getting more young people into work.
“The Government should act on this recommendation at the earliest opportunity and recognise hospitality for what it is; not simply a great place for young people to start their careers, but a willing and essential partner in tackling one of the biggest employment challenges facing the country.”
Lower youth pay ‘vital’
Pano Christou, chief executive of Pret A Manger, said Milburn’s call to cut employer NICs “is a welcome step in encouraging employers to hire young people into the industry”.
Rob Swain, the general manager of KFC UK, said Milburn’s recommendations were welcome but added that “getting people into work is only half the job”.
The government should reform the Apprenticeship Levy, which is charged to employers to fund training, to release more funds to employers, according to Milburn’s recommendations. The government currently retains about £460m of this levy, according to the review.
“The Milburn Review rightly focuses on opening the first door, but we also need to make sure young people are ready to step through it and are supported to stay and progress,” Swain said.
Retailers have also urged the government to reduce the number of Neets in Britain by cutting national insurance and retaining a lower minimum wage for young people.
Labour had committed to eradicating “discriminatory” aged-based pay gaps but Milburn said businesses will be deterred from hiring young people if they are required to pay them the same wage as older, more experienced workers.
“The priority must be to keep the first rung open while protecting fair pay. The young person needs to be able to get on the first rung of the career ladder before they can then climb it,” Milburn said.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the British Retail Consortium, which represents grocers including Tesco and Sainsbury’s, said retaining a lower minimum wage to get Neets into work was “vital”.
“Young people with little or no experience already face an uphill battle competing with more experienced candidates, and the last thing they need is anything that makes that first step into employment even harder,” she said.

items.title: Santander allows staff to count holidays and sick leave as days worked in office
items.summary: News of Spanish-owned lender’s policy emerges as other banks are toughening their stance on working from home Business live – latest updates Staff at the high street bank Santander have been permitted to log holiday and sick leave as days worked in the office, helping them to meet workplace attendance requirements. Back-office staff at the Spanish-owned lender have been expected to spend at least 12 working days each month in what the company calls a “head office location”, although this does not apply to staff working in bank branches. Continue reading...
items.body:
Staff at the high street bank Santander have been permitted to log holiday and sick leave as days worked in the office, helping them to meet workplace attendance requirements.
Back-office staff at the Spanish-owned lender have been expected to spend at least 12 working days each month in what the company calls a “head office location”, although this does not apply to staff working in bank branches.
However, at the same time as other banks are toughening their stance on the rights of employees to work from home, it has emerged that a peculiarity in the lender’s system means that workers are marked as being at their desk even when they are on annual leave or off work because of illness.
The company has its UK headquarters in Milton Keynes, England, and has offices in Glasgow and central London.
This means that any staff member taking a two-week holiday would be logged as spending 10 days that month working in the office, meaning they would only need to attend another two days over two weeks, making the office attendance rules less strict than they first appear.
A spokesperson for Santander told the Times, which first reported the story, said: “The 12 days a month requirement is adjusted for periods of leave, including public holidays, annual leave and sick leave (meaning if a colleague is not well enough to work, they do not have to make up their in-office days).
“Our policy allows for collaboration and enables colleagues to develop, while providing flexibility to suit individual needs.”
Santander formalised hybrid working arrangements that had been in place since the pandemic in September 2024, joining a range of other banks in toughening up its remote working policy.
Its previous guidance permitted employees to spend two or three days each week in the office and the rest of the time working from home.
Santander’s former UK chief executive, Mike Regnier, was one of the proponents of hybrid working, telling the Guardian that he wouldn’t have accepted the role had he not been permitted to spend at least one day a week at his desk in his family home in Yorkshire.
Despite this, Regnier said at the time he hoped the new campus-style headquarters in Milton Keynes would attract workers back to their desks more frequently.
Meanwhile, the bank said Regnier’s successor, Mahesh Aditya, who took over in March, would spend five days a week in the office, amid Santander’s work to integrate the high street lender TSB, which it bought last year for £2.65bn.
In a sign of the ongoing battle between staff and employers over the right to continued working from home, staff unions reacted angrily to NatWest’s October announcement it was ordering 13,000 staff back to the office for two days a week, up from two days a month.
From February 2027, nearly all of the 40,000 UK staff working for its Royal Bank of Scotland, NatWest, Ulster Bank and Coutts brands will be required to spend more days at their desks, ending a remote-first policy for thousands of employees.

items.body:
Some of the biggest names in the meat alternatives market, including Quorn, Linda McCartney Foods, Beyond Meat and THIS, have chosen the Vegetarian Society’s trusted product certification to demonstrate their commitment to vegetarian, vegan and plant-based standards.
As the meat alternatives market continues to evolve, consumer confidence and clear product labelling have never been more important. The Vegetarian Society works with leading manufacturers across the sector, providing independent product certification that helps consumers make informed choices with confidence.
The Vegetarian Society Certification Scheme offers three internationally recognised certification marks: Vegetarian Approved, Vegan Approved and Plant Based Approved. Uniquely, the Society is the only organisation in its field to offer all three, enabling manufacturers to demonstrate their products’ credentials to a broad range of consumers, whatever their dietary preferences or purchasing motivations.
From dedicated vegetarians and vegans to flexitarians and those simply looking to incorporate more plant-based foods into their diets, the certification marks provide clear, trusted reassurance at the point of purchase.
For manufacturers, certification offers more than a recognisable mark on packaging. It provides independent verification of product ingredients and production processes, helping brands build consumer trust, strengthen their market positioning and reach new audiences.
With decades of experience in food certification, the Vegetarian Society continues to work alongside established household names and emerging brands, supporting the growth and development of the vegetarian, vegan and plant-based food market.
Said Nina Anderson, head of corporate sales at the Vegetarian Society, said: “YouGov research shows that 82% of vegetarian and vegan consumers would prefer to see our accreditation symbol on product packaging, rather than reading through an ingredient list. Our role is to provide manufacturers with trusted, independent accreditation while giving consumers the confidence to choose products that align with their values and dietary preference.”

Graham Eyes has ‘steaked’ his place in the digital world with the launch of a new online butchery website. Customers can visit www.grahameyesbutchers.co.uk to select their fresh meat through the new click and collect service, choosing to pick up their order at any one of the 24 Graham Eyes butchers counters located within Spar stores across […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Graham Eyes has ‘steaked’ his place in the digital world with the launch of a new online butchery website. Customers can visit www.grahameyesbutchers.co.uk to select their fresh meat through the new click and collect service, choosing to pick up their order at any one of the 24 Graham Eyes butchers counters located within Spar stores across the North of England.
The development has been launched in time for Christmas ordering enabling customers to get ahead of the Christmas rush, organise their festive shopping early, and enjoy greater peace of mind as December approaches.
Included in the range are Christmas hampers, family sized joints of meat, a selection of game products, and trimmings and accompaniments to suit different households and celebratory occasions.
There is also the option to enquire about bespoke catering opportunities delivered by Graham Eyes’ expert butchery event team.
Graham Eyes said: “Our new website combines the convenience of online shopping with the quality and service of a traditional butcher. It looks fantastic and is easy to use too – all this while continuing support for a local butcher which is important.
“Customers can feast their eyes on our selection of quality meats and traditional Christmas favourites in their own time and from the comfort of their home These cater to different price points, giving people the chance secure their festive meals within a budget that suits.
“The online pre-order service offers customers a handy way to organise Christmas meat and festive essentials ahead of time which eases the pressure on Christmas to-do lists.”
Graham Eyes began his butchery journey in 1982, opening his first shop on Rufford Road in Southport at just 21 years old.
Over the years, he has built a reputation for quality meat, traditional sausage making, and homemade products, becoming a much-loved name in the local community in and around Southport.
In 2016, Graham partnered with James Hall & Co. Ltd, bringing Graham Eyes butchery counters into SPAR stores across the North of England. In the process, it has ensured quality, locally supplied meat products are accessible to even more communities.
James Hall & Co. Ltd is a fifth-generation family business which serves a network of independent SPAR retailers and company-owned SPAR stores across Northern England six days a week from its base at Bowland View in Preston.

British retailers are doubling down on Black Friday discounts, with new PayPal research among 1,000 UK e-commerce decision-makers revealing that almost all (98%) consider promotions important to achieving their online sales targets, while 85% expect to rely more heavily on discounts and promotions this Christmas than last year. This emphasis on promotions reflects a wider […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
British retailers are doubling down on Black Friday discounts, with new PayPal research among 1,000 UK e-commerce decision-makers revealing that almost all (98%) consider promotions important to achieving their online sales targets, while 85% expect to rely more heavily on discounts and promotions this Christmas than last year.
This emphasis on promotions reflects a wider focus on attracting shoppers. More than four in five (82%) UK ecommerce decision-makers say their businesses place greater priority on customer acquisition than improving the checkout experience during peak trading.
But consumers are thinking about more than price. Separate PayPal research found that 53% of UK adults start considering how they’ll pay by the time they’re browsing products, including 26% before they even visit a retailer’s website.
Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) is one example of why payment visibility matters. A third (33%) of UK adults have used or plan to use BNPL for Christmas shopping this year. Among those who have already used it, 55% would favour a retailer displaying the option on product pages, compared with 21% favouring one that waits until checkout.
However, checkout remains the most reported individual location for UK businesses offering BNPL to communicate its availability, with 40% displaying the option there before customers select a payment method.
Retailers are already exploring earlier payment visibility. Among UK businesses offering BNPL, 65% have moved or tested moving messaging earlier in the shopping journey.
Sean Douglas, head of UK large enterprise at PayPal, said: “Black Friday shouldn’t become a race to the bottom on price. Retailers work incredibly hard to attract shoppers, but getting customers onto their websites is only half the battle.
“Our research found that 92% of UK retailers who moved or tested moving BNPL messaging earlier reported increased conversion rates. For businesses, that’s a compelling reason to look beyond discounts and consider how making payment options visible earlier could help turn interest into sales.”
PayPal’s own data also points to the commercial benefits of earlier payment visibility. In the UK, merchants introducing Pay Later messaging earlier in the shopping journey saw a 6.9% increase in payment volumes through PayPal. When combined with an additional PayPal payment button, that increase rose to 11%.³
Retailers can make PayPal Pay Later visible earlier in the shopping journey, including on product pages, helping eligible customers understand their payment options before checkout. Businesses can find guidance on adding and optimising Pay Later messaging through the PayPal Pay Later Messaging Centre.

items.title: REWE pulls plug on its Trigo technology powered Pick & Go autonomous store project
items.summary: REWE Group is ending its Pick & Go autonomous store project. The German retailer has been working on this with Trigo since 2021, tapping computer vision cameras to enable people to shop and go and not have to deal with traditional checkouts.In a LinkedIn post, REWE Group's Chief Digital & Te
items.body:
REWE Group is ending its Pick & Go autonomous store project. The German retailer has been working on this with Trigo since 2021, tapping computer vision cameras to enable people to shop and go and not have to deal with traditional checkouts.
In a LinkedIn post, REWE Group's Chief Digital & Technology Officer, Christoph Eltze, said: "The future of checkout is not determined by a single technology. A large supermarket has different requirements than a small convenience location or a local supply service. And our customers also have different needs depending on the purchase. That's why we have been testing a wide variety of technological solutions and store concepts for years: from self-checkout and automated checkout processes to largely autonomous stores."
He added: "Our standard is not whether a technology is particularly new or spectacular. What matters is whether it makes shopping easier for our customers and proves itself in real operation. Testing is therefore an essential part of our self-understanding. With clear learning objectives and openness to different outcomes. Because not every test has to be continued exactly as it started. What matters is what we can learn from it and use elsewhere."
In seven Pick & Go markets in Germany, REWE Group tested computer vision in a day to day store environment over a long period of time. In doing so, it says that it learned a lot about how customers use automated checkout and what requirements the technology must meet in daily operations.
Eltze commented: "We have achieved the learning objectives we set for ourselves in advance. That is precisely why the operational testing phase in these seven markets is now ending, and the evaluation of the insights gained is beginning to decide what further developments we can derive from them."
"What is important to me is that the end of this testing phase is not the end of our engagement with computer vision. On the contrary. We also further test and develop various applications and concepts for automated and autonomous shopping elsewhere. Because it's not about finding a technology for the future of checkout. The goal is to find out which solution offers our customers the greatest added value in which purchasing situation. That's why we test. That's what we learn for. And from that, we continue to develop. This is exactly how reliable decisions are made for tomorrow's trade."
REWE Group becomes the latest high profile retailer to walk away from the autonomous store concept, and it was arguably the most noteworthy user of the technology after Amazon Go went kaput last year.
So, is this the end of the road for autonomous grocery stores, due to the ROI just not being there? Or is there life in the not so old dog yet? Let us know your thoughts in the comments section below.
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Autonomous stores were a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our winners were revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
The event consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.

items.title: Give stores more help if you want to preserve banking services, ACS tells government
items.summary: The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) has issued a fresh warning that the government needs to help local shops offer banking services if it wants to maintain access to banking where traditional banks have closed branches. The renewed warning comes in the wake of the… This story continues at Give stores more help if you want to preserve banking services, ACS tells government Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The renewed warning comes in the wake of the Access to Banking Review, which recommends new legal protections to make sure people can continue to access the face-to-face banking services they need.
The review says more than three million people rely on face-to-face banking, rising to more than four million when less-frequent users are included.
This is particularly important for older people, disabled people, people on low incomes, those facing negative life events, and those who find digital services harder to use, as they may face difficulties accessing banking online.
ACS chief executive Ed Woodall said: “The future of access to banking will increasingly depend on local shops being able to provide these vital services in their communities.
“The government cannot take the delivery of these services by local shops for granted.
“Providing face-to-face banking services means employing skilled people and operating premises, which is becoming increasingly more expensive for retailers.
“If government is serious about protecting access to banking, it needs to make sure the businesses delivering these services are supported.”
ACS research shows more than one in four consumers use their local shop for Post Office services, 22% to withdraw cash, and 8% to pay bills over the counter or to top up their electricity.

At the heart of the series is the idea that rugby is more than the game, celebrating […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
British menswear brand Charles Tyrwhitt, the exclusive formalwear partner of England Rugby, is bringing its partnership with the team to life with a new social-first campaign, celebrating what makes rugby about more than the game on the pitch.
At the heart of the series is the idea that rugby is more than the game, celebrating the friendships, personalities and shared experiences that bring a team together. Filmed at Pennyhill Park, the training base and home of England Rugby, Tommy Freeman, Max Ojomoh and George Martin step away from their usual training routines to take on challenges that put their skills, knowledge and team relationships to the test.
Kicking off with The Great Rugby Steak-Off, a surf-and-turf cooking competition judged by Pennyhill Park’s chef, the players offer a more personal glimpse into life behind the scenes. Through candid conversations, friendly rivalry and plenty of laughs, the series captures the camaraderie that exists beyond match day, highlighting the people behind the players and what makes being part of the England squad about so much more than the game itself.
Alongside the films, the campaign also features a social competition giving fans the chance to win tickets to see England take on New Zealand at the Nations Championship, bringing supporters closer to the action.
The campaign coincides with the launch of 11 new pieces in Charles Tyrwhitt’s official rugby collection, bringing together the brand’s menswear expertise and longstanding relationship with England Rugby. New additions include an England Rugby Pure Merino Zip-Neck Jumper (RRP £59.95), a Navy Long Sleeve Smart Piqué Polo (RRP £69.95), and the England Rugby Striped Socks (RRP £12.95). Combining everyday wardrobe staples with subtle England Rugby detailing, the collection offers supporters new ways to show their team colours both on and off the pitch.
Entering its seventh year as the official formalwear partner of the RFU, Charles Tyrwhitt continues to celebrate its connection with rugby through activity that goes beyond match day, recognising the people, relationships and moments that make the sport what it is.

items.body:
This Christmas, John Lewis introduces the ‘Drop Shop’ – a destination for limited-edition product launches. Starting on 3 December, there will be six exclusive releases spanning streetwear-inspired bed linen, collectables and toys, beauty, home and audio, with a new drop landing every other day…
The lineup pairs cult favourites with unexpected firsts. No Problemo takes its extraterrestrial universe into bedding. POP MART’s Hot Pot Collection makes its European debut. Le Creuset gives collectors a UK&I exclusive in Berry. Marshall puts original artwork on its speakers, Trinny London delivers an exclusive beauty edit, and Nothing (R) pushes red to the extreme. All products only available at John Lewis.
Each release lands first in-store in three selected locations: Oxford Street, Edinburgh and Liverpool. Drops will then be available on JohnLewis.com and the John Lewis App the following day. With zero restocks and limited availability, shoppers will need to act quickly. The sixth and final drop arrives in-store on 13 December.
At John Lewis Oxford Street, the lineup goes beyond the products. Expect a live performance from The Molotovs, an exclusive in-store experience with Trinny Woodall, and live DJ hosted by Nothing (R) and Foundation FM. Come for the drop. Stay for what happens next.
John Lewis Drop Shop gives shoppers six new dates to circle, with one-of-a-kind releases landing alongside live performances and special experiences. Each drop offers a fresh reason to visit John Lewis this December.
Jason Wilary-Attew, director of home at John Lewis, said: “For generations, John Lewis has been at the heart of Christmas gifting. This year, we’re combining that trusted festive magic with the energy and anticipation of drop culture. Drop Shop brings together brilliant brands, exclusive releases and unexpected experiences, giving customers new reasons to get excited about finding something special this Christmas.”
SET YOUR ALARM:
- Thursday, 3 December | Opening Timings 10am – 9pm No Problemo takes bedding into its orbit No Problemo’s next destination? Your bedroom. The British streetwear label debuts in bedding, with exclusive duvet and pillow sets and throws designed for John Lewis Drop Shop. Drawing on its extraterrestrial world and fascination with UFO folklore, the collection translates the label’s cult streetwear aesthetic into something worth coming home for. The extra enticement? Limited gifts up for grabs with purchase, whilst stocks last. Consider your Christmas hibernation sorted. Prices starting from: £55
- Saturday, 5 December | Opening Timings 10am – 9pm POP MART’s Hot Pot collectables serve European exclusives Serving up your next collecting obsession. POP MART’s Hot Pot Collection makes its European debut, reimagining fan favourites including LABUBU, SKULLPANDA, CRYBABY, DIMOO and MOLLY as playful hot pot ingredients. Available in blind boxes and as individual collectables, the plush designs feature details ranging from squeakers and clips to magnetic parts and detachable accessories. Pick your favourites, hunt for hidden characters and make room in your collection. Prices starting from: £21
- Monday, 7 December | Opening Timings 10am – 9pm Marshall turns up the volume with customized speakers by Creative Studio ARE YOU MAD and guest performances by The Molotovs Marshall gives its Acton IV Black speaker three exclusive graffiti art designs by creative studio Are You Mad: Lightning, Stars and Doodle. Artistic hand painted craft meets rich, expansive sound, with exclusive custom laser engraving by Are You Mad at John Lewis Oxford Street adding a personal touch. And if that was exciting enough, Marshall Records’ own The Molotovs will take over the Oxford Street shop floor for two explosive live performances at 11am and 6pm. Expect the London duo’s energetic collision of mod, punk and rock and roll, bringing raw live energy to the heart of Christmas shopping. Get there for the drop. Stay for the gig, take the music home with you. Prices starting from: £259
- Wednesday, 9 December | Opening Timings 10am – 9pm Le Creuset gives collectors a new crush Le Creuset brings a burst of Berry to John Lewis Drop Shop this December, with a curated capsule of five cast iron pieces exclusive to John Lewis in the UK. Inspired by freshly picked berries, the vivid blend of fuchsia, rose and lilac is finished with a gold leaf shimmer, bringing a fresh flourish to festive tables. The Traditional Flower Dish takes centre stage, with an embossed floral lid inspired by the French anemone. At Oxford Street, oversized berries take over Drop Shop, with personalisation available to add a thoughtful finishing touch to Christmas gifting. Those lucky enough to be the first through the door to purchase their new ‘Berry crush’, can grab a Berry Christmas wreath as a special gift. Prices starting from: £265
- Friday, 11 December | Opening Timings 10am – 9pm Trinny Woodall brings her beauty expertise to Oxford Street Trinny London’s festive edit has landed. The cult British brand has curated an exclusive gift set available only at Drop Shop, combining the award-winning Take Back Time eye treatment with a stackable mini of the bestselling neck and décolleté concentrate, The Elevator. Completed with sculpting stainless steel Cryo Globes and a limited edition holographic Atlantic case, this showstopper is designed to target where visible changes show first – lifting, firming, and bringing back that vital spark. Bringing her infectious energy and straight-talking beauty advice to Drop Shop, Trinny Woodall is set to appear at John Lewis Oxford Street for a festive beauty takeover, with exclusive appointments and in-store experiences. Prices starting from: £120
- Sunday, 13 Dec | Opening Timings 12noon – 6 pm Nothing (R) pushes red to the extreme Nothing (R) brings its distinct design language to John Lewis Drop Shop with a limited edition red case for its new Headphone (1) Pro. Usually a signature accent, the Nothing (R) Red becomes the main event. The headphones pair transparent design with studio-level audio. To celebrate, Nothing (R) takes over John Lewis Drop Shop Oxford Street, with Foundation FM streaming live DJ sets from artists who embody experimentation. Prices starting from: £349
Drop Shop will launch from 3 – 13 December 2026, with products dropping in-store at
John Lewis Oxford Street, Edinburgh and Liverpool with consumer experiences, then onto johnlewis.com throughout December.

With Black Friday just a few weeks away, DPD has opened seven new parcel depots to support the 2026 peak […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
The UK’s leading premium parcel delivery company DPD is gearing up for an expected record peak period with more electric vehicles (EVs) on the road, more delivery drivers and more parcel depots than ever before.
With Black Friday just a few weeks away, DPD has opened seven new parcel depots to support the 2026 peak push and the ongoing growth in parcel volumes through into next year and beyond.
The new sites in Croydon, Derby, Doncaster, Eastleigh, Norwich, Stockport and Worcester range from 21,000 sq ft to 83,000 sq ft and all are now open and operational. The new locations follow the opening of three giant purpose-built and fully automated distribution centres earlier this year in Crawley, Darlington and Sittingbourne.
DPD has also confirmed it will have a record number of EVs on the road this Christmas, with over 720 new Mercedes-Benz e-Sprinter and Ford E-Transit vans helping deliver Christmas in a more sustainable way across the UK.
DPD’s year-round seven day a week, next-day delivery service will operate as normal up to and including Christmas Eve, to ensure customer parcels get where they need to be on time.
Justin Pegg, DPD UK CEOm commented: “We know just how critical peak is for our customers and every year we pull out all the stops to deliver for them. Talking to customers we know this Black Friday and Christmas is going to be huge, so we have ramped up the capacity right across our network. We are a seven day a week, next-day delivery operation all year round but at this time of year, that constant throughput at weekends can make a huge difference both in terms of shippers getting the goods into their customer’s hands and for us in terms of handling the busiest peak days effectively. As the UK’s leading premium carrier our customers count on quality service, industry leading innovation and sustainable business practices and our plan for peak 2026 is focused on delivering for those customers when it matters most.”
Details on all of DPD’s sustainability initiatives can be found on its dedicated website.

items.body:
Ribble has widened its nationwide retail footprint further through its successful partnership with Cotswold Outdoor, launching two new dedicated concepts within their stores at Chertsey and Rushden Lakes. The dual opening follows Ribble’s launch in Newcastle city centre last month and its initial space in Leeds in May.
The new locations can be found inside Cotswold Outdoor, 99 Fordwater Road, Chertsey (KT16 8HH) and Cotswold Outdoor, Unit D2 Rushden Lakes Shopping Centre (NN10 6FW).
Both locations give riders direct access to Ribble’s Road, Gravel, Hybrid, and Electric ranges, supported by in-house specialists offering sizing, geometry, and build guidance. Customers can test bikes, configure bespoke componentry builds and CustomColour finishes, and collect fully assembled bikes in-store, complete with a 30-day free test ride and lifetime frame and fork warranty.
To mark the Surrey launch, the Chertsey store is displaying a one-off 2024 ALLROAD SLR from Ribble’s custom archive. Finished in white marble with gold leaf detailing and exposed carbon fibre, it offers visitors an up-close look at the level of detail possible on a bespoke Ribble build.
At Rushden Lakes, visitors can get an up-close look at an ALLGRIT E Carbon X built with SRAM Rival XPLR AXS. Finished in one of Ribble’s signature colour-flip paints, it pairs the brand’s performance e-gravel bike with its CustomColour offering.
Sean Hastings, CEO at Ribble, said: “The fantastic response we’ve had to our spaces in Leeds and Newcastle has proved there is a huge appetite for riders to get hands-on with our bikes, and learn more about them. Partnering with Cotswold Outdoor once again to open in Chertsey and Rushden Lakes is all about making it easier for riders to reach us, bringing world-class British bikes directly to cycling communities across the country.”
Jamie Kristow, CEO at Cotswold Outdoor, said: “At Cotswold Outdoor, we’re passionate about getting people outdoors with the right equipment for every adventure. We’re delighted to expand our partnership with Ribble, bringing its high-performance bikes to our Chertsey and Rushden Lakes stores. Customers will be able to visit these stores to explore the Ribble range, talk to knowledgeable specialists and discover a truly personalised build.”
Every Ribble is designed and built to order in the UK. Tried, tested and proven in British conditions since 1897. By the riders who know them best, from everyday cyclists to Yorkshire-based champions like Jenson Young and Harry Tanfield.
To find out more about both of these openings, visit:
ribblecycles.co.uk/rushden-bike-store/ and ribblecycles.co.uk/chertsey-bike-store/

items.title: Ikea ditches plans for new UK stores, blaming high business taxes
items.summary: Retailer’s British boss says John Healey ‘missed opportunity to back retailers’ in October’s budget Business live – latest updates Ikea has ditched some planned store openings in the UK blaming the cost of business taxes , which it said were the highest in Europe. As its annual UK sales little more than flatlined at the Swedish flatpack furniture retailer, its UK boss, David McCabe, said: “There are locations where we were planning to open a new unit, and those plans have been abandoned due to the cost that we experience and the complexity within the market. Continue reading...
items.body:
Ikea has ditched some planned store openings in the UK blaming the cost of business taxes, which it said were the highest in Europe.
As its annual UK sales little more than flatlined at the Swedish flatpack furniture retailer, its UK boss, David McCabe, said: “There are locations where we were planning to open a new unit, and those plans have been abandoned due to the cost that we experience and the complexity within the market.
“I would hope that we’re able to bring those projects back to life,” he added. “But it’s a very real impact here in the UK, when those investments will go to other countries in Europe.”
The planned investments were smaller UK stores, but the retailer declined to comment on exact locations. Ikea has been pushing further into smaller high street shops, rather than its traditional out-of-town outlets.
Ikea’s UK arm pays the most business taxes of its operations in Europe, and the third highest in the world, after the US and China, he said.
The retailer’s UK sales edged 0.5% higher to £2.26bn in the year to the end of August. Sales rose 4.7% in the first four months of the year but fell in the second half as weak confidence and “sustained pressure” on household budgets led consumers to pull back on big purchases.
McCabe said he had talked to customers in stores in recent weeks who were planning to replace an entire bedroom, but then decided to just buy one or two smaller pieces of furniture and a refresh with new textiles to save money.
“We are seeing a change in the way that customers shop and we do anticipate a difficult period going forward,” he said. “We don’t think that there’s going to be a sudden, miraculous turnaround in confidence.”
McCabe described John Healey’s recent budget as a “missed opportunity to back retailers under real pressure”, but said Ikea continued to talk to the government.
The company has spent £54m on reducing prices by an average of 20% on 425 products, including its popular Billy bookcase, Hemnes daybed and the cantilever Poäng armchair.
Ikea is using seasonal offers to pull in customers, for example discounts on extendable dining tables, folding chairs and soft toys in the run-up to Christmas.
McCabe said smaller stores, between 1,000 and 2,000 sq metres, had been popular with customers, in sites such as Oxford Street in London and retail parks.
As well as the Oxford Street shop which opened within the former Topshop flagship site, Ikea opened stores in Brighton, Norwich and York last year, followed by a small store in Chester. It also opened a “plan and order” site – dedicated to kitchen, bedroom, and living room planning – in Dundee, and one in Aberdeen last month.

items.title: Boden selects OneStock to power its US expansion and wholesale growth with unified order orchestration
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. British fashion brand, Boden, has selected OneStock, the leading Distributed Order Management (DOM) platform, to unify its inventory and order flows as it accelerates U.S. expansion and scales its international Direct To Consumer (DTC) and wholesale operations. Founded as a mail-order catalogue in the 1990s, Boden first launched its ecommerce channel in 2000 and last […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
British fashion brand, Boden, has selected OneStock, the leading Distributed Order Management (DOM) platform, to unify its inventory and order flows as it accelerates U.S. expansion and scales its international Direct To Consumer (DTC) and wholesale operations.
Founded as a mail-order catalogue in the 1990s, Boden first launched its ecommerce channel in 2000 and last year posted £387million in omnichannel revenues, selling in over 50 countries worldwide.  While much of the fashion retailer’s sales are generated online, the brand is also focused on growing its wholesale footprint and physical retail network internationally.
Last year, the U.S. was Boden’s fastest-growing market, accounting for almost half of group revenue.  Already scaling its wholesale business with American department stores including Nordstrom, Boden also opened its first U.S. stores in Atlanta (Nov 2025), Nashville (Jul 2026) and Alabama (Nov 2026) as its international estate grows at pace.
To support its ambitious expansion plans, Boden recognised the need to modernise its Order Management System (OMS), seeking a centralised platform to allow it to manage increasingly complex order flows, segment stock and scale seamlessly.
As well as its proven track record in DTC fashion, including partnerships with JD Sports Fashion, Orlebar Brown, Jigsaw and Longchamp, OneStock was also selected for its native Shopify integration, which allowed Boden – one of Shopify’s largest EMEA clients – to reduce technical complexities for seamless implementation.
“As we look to grow the business through international expansion, particularly in the U.S., and adding new channels like wholesale and retail, we need more sophisticated order orchestration capabilities to support these ambitions,” said Alexander Ives, senior director of technology at Boden.
“OneStock will bring our order orchestration together into a single platform, giving us the flexibility we need to support the business whichever direction it wants to take.  This means we’ll be able to continue managing a single pool of stock while dynamically altering what we display to different channels, this will enable us to deliver seamless shopping journeys, while building the operational foundations to support our next phase of growth,” Ives added.
A phased rollout will see OneStock supporting Boden’s DTC operations, orchestrating orders from its UK, North American and European Shopify storefronts, as well as its marketplace channels and new U.S. stores.  This will bring delivery promises at checkout and returns management together on one central platform, providing a unified view of stock across all channels.  With greater visibility of product availability, Boden will be better positioned to respond to surges in demand, minimise stock-outs and enhance its customer experience.
OneStock will also support Boden’s growing wholesale channel, including an intelligent stock reservation and reallocation system, which keeps inventory set aside for specific wholesale partners.  OneStock will also allow Boden to scale its wholesale operations, moving from writing code to add new wholesale partners to configuring OneStock, to dramatically reduce the time to market for implementing new relationships.
“Retailers are increasingly operating in a Promise Economy,” said Romulus Grigoras, CEO and co-founder of OneStock. “And that means giving customers confidence that the commitments made at the point of purchase will be fulfilled, every time – whether they’re an individual shopper or a wholesale partner.”
“By unifying inventory and intelligently orchestrating orders across channels, Boden can extend the same precision, reliability and transparency of delivery promises to its wholesale partners as its DTC customers, ensuring every promise made is a promise kept,” he added.

items.body:
Leading accessible health and beauty retailer Superdrug is giving away thousands of beauty products across the UK as it gives customers the royal treatment this National Princess Day, 18th November.
As part of the celebrations, a number of princesses will swap their palaces for Superdrug stores from Edinburgh to Cardiff and Manchester to London, welcoming customers in-store for a day of fairytale beauty.
They will be joined by make-up artists on hand to give customers their own princess-inspired look. From icy blues and midnight sparkle to enchanted greens and rose-pink romance, customers can experiment with a new look and discover their new beauty favourites, with expertly applied make-up using accessible products and tips on recreating the look at home.
As an extra royal treat, the princesses will hand out free beauty bundles to customers after their make-up experience, with 100 available at each participating store. Worth over £60 each and packed with ten make-up and beauty essentials, the bundles feature a Studio London four-piece base set, Radiance primer, Glow Get It highlighter and gold eyeshadow pigment, alongside a pink cosmetics bag and more.

items.title: Former WH Smith chain TG Jones put up for sale after closing 130 stores
items.summary: Modella Capital plans auction of high street retailer, which employs about 3,500 people, next year Business live – latest updates The owner of TG Jones is exploring a potential sale less than 18 months after completing a deal to buy the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith. Modella Capital, which also owns businesses including Hobbycraft, completed a deal to buy the 233-year-old business for £42m in June last year. Continue reading...
items.body:
The owner of TG Jones is exploring a potential sale less than 18 months after completing a deal to buy the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith.
Modella Capital, which also owns businesses including Hobbycraft, completed a deal to buy the 233-year-old business for £42m in June last year.
The company, which pushed through a swingeing restructure to close more than 100 stores after receiving high court approval in July, has moved to appoint advisers after receiving unsolicited expressions of interest for the business.
Modella, which has closed about 150 of the 480 WH Smith stores since taking control, has appointed the corporate finance arm of Teneo, according to Sky News which first reported the news.
“High-street retailer TG Jones has received unsolicited offers for the business,” said Modella and TG Jones in a joint statement. “Management and owner Modella Capital have jointly agreed to instruct Teneo Corporate Finance to review these offers and undertake a market-testing exercise.”
An auction of the business, which employs about 3,500 staff, is planned for next year to avoid disruption through the key Christmas trading period.
“As ever, our focus is on providing a great experience for customers, especially with the critical Christmas period coming up,” said the TG Jones chief executive, Alex Wilson. “We continue to execute our turnaround plan, which is improving our performance month by month.”
WH Smith retained its almost 1,300 stores in train stations and airports, as well as its website and the right to its name, promoting the rebrand of the high street stores to TG Jones.
The potential sale comes as the future of Poundland, which employs approximately 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, remains uncertain.
Last week the chain’s owner, Gordon Brothers, won approval from the high court for an extension of legal protection from creditors as it assesses three potential bids.
Last month its US owners filed a notice of intention to call in administrators, but has come under pressure to accept a bid for the company that would save retail jobs and protect thousands of suppliers.

items.body:
Online running shoes, clothing and outdoor gear retailer SportsShoes.com has announced six new appointments to support its ongoing growth strategy.
The new hires are across SportsShoes.com’s events, marketing, customer relationship management and social media specialisms.
Established in 1982, Bradford-based SportsShoes.com offers customers in the UK, Europe and Scandinavia more than 15,000 products from 150 global running and outdoor brands.
Outdoor brands include The North Face, Salomon, Montane, Rab and Patagonia, while its running portfolio features Asics, Nike, Adidas, Hoka, New Balance and Brooks.
Marie Cheng joins SportsShoes.com as its first event operations manager, having previously held roles as marketing and communications manager at Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) UK and digital marketing manager at Ourea Events.
She will lead the delivery of SportsShoes.com’s expanding programme of races, community events and brand partner activities. Marie is also an active trail runner and has taken part in the UTMB World Series Finals.
Hannah Cawthra has been hired as marketing executive for trail and outdoors, joining from Hoka. A keen trail and ultramarathon runner, Hannah has completed endurance events including the 100km CCC race at UTMB Mont-Blanc and Ultra-Trail Snowdonia.
The customer relationship management (CRM) team has been strengthened with the appointments of Emily Coleman from Gym King, and Ryan Malpas from agri-food science company Fera. Both join SportsShoes.com as CRM executives.
Georgie Gilbert has been appointed as social lead, having previously held senior roles at footwear magazine Sneaker Freaker International and UK brands house Apparel Brands Group.
Completing the new appointments is Tom Lawrenson, who joins as a senior performance executive from The SEO Works.
Welcoming the new appointments, Dan Cartner, head of marketing at SportsShoes.com, said: “Our ambition to be unrivalled in running means getting front and centre of the communities we serve.
“Marie, Hannah, Ryan, Emily, Georgie and Tom will help us build those connections. Marie and Hannah’s personal experiences in trail running also give them first-hand insight into the sport and an understanding of what matters to the people taking part.
“As our events programme expands and the business grows, our team has an important role in giving more people reasons to get involved with SportsShoes.com.
“These appointments will help us do that, from bringing runners together at races to sharing useful, inspiring content and making our customer communications more relevant.”
For further information on the retailer, visit www.sportsshoes.com

items.summary: The Entertainer has unveiled its 2026 Christmas campaign, Play. Their Way, encouraging shoppers to embrace children’s imaginations when choosing festive gifts. The campaign, which launches today, sees children rewrite the rules of Christmas, turning everyday spaces into playgrounds and encouraging adults to join in the fun. Its hero advert opens with a parent asking four...
items.body:
The Entertainer has unveiled its 2026 Christmas campaign, Play. Their Way, encouraging shoppers to embrace children’s imaginations when choosing festive gifts.
The campaign, which launches today, sees children rewrite the rules of Christmas, turning everyday spaces into playgrounds and encouraging adults to join in the fun.
Its hero advert opens with a parent asking four children to keep the living room tidy, only for them to transform it into a racetrack, dress-up area and play space, with even Brussels sprouts becoming targets for remote-controlled cars.
The campaign will run across social media, out-of-home advertising, digital, radio and the toy chain’s 160 stores.
Research from The Entertainer found that 60 per cent of parents have taken over building or making something because they were enjoying it themselves, while 53 per cent admitted playing with their children’s toys after bedtime.
The Entertainer group chief customer officer Craig Inglis said: “Children have a brilliant ability to find play in the everyday. They ask unexpected questions, make up their own rules and see possibilities that grown-ups can easily miss.”
He added: “With Play. Their Way, we want to celebrate that imagination and remind everyone to make a little more room for play this Christmas. Whatever your age, the best gifts are the ones that tap into how you love to play.”
The campaign was created by communications agency PrettyGreen, with media planning and buying handled by OMD.
PrettyGreen strategy and creative managing partner Lucy Porter said: “The idea started with a simple truth: children instinctively see more possibilities for play than adults do.”

items.title: Modella Capital puts former WH Smith stores TG Jones up for sale
items.summary: Modella Capital has kicked off a sale of TG Jones, the high street business that formerly traded as WH Smith, less than two years into its ownership. The private equity firm has called in advisors at Teneo to oversee an auction of the retail business, which includes about 350 shops and 3,500 workers, in the [...]
items.body:
Modella Capital puts former WH Smith stores TG Jones up for sale
Modella Capital has kicked off a sale of TG Jones, the high street business that formerly traded as WH Smith, less than two years into its ownership.
The private equity firm has called in advisors at Teneo to oversee an auction of the retail business, which includes about 350 shops and 3,500 workers, in the weeks running up to Christmas.
Modella had not been proactively seeking a deal but decided to trigger an auction after receiving unsolicited expressions of interest in buying the business, it is understood.
The process will take place in the coming weeks, but a transaction would not take place until after Christmas, in the first quarter of next year, sources close to the matter told City AM.
The group snapped up WH Smith’s 480 high street shops for an initial £10m in June last year and later pushed through a divisive restructuring plan which it claimed was necessary to ensure the retailer’s survival. The turnaround plan, opposed by landlords who objected to proposals to slash the rent paid by TG Jones, triggered the closure of up to 150 of the retailer’s sites.
Modella faced criticism for its early stewardship of the former WH Smith shops, after it rebranded each site with new TG Jones branding and charged royalties for the new moniker.
The private equity firm believes it has set the retailer back on the right course since taking over, with one person close to Modella saying it is now a “viable but smaller” business.
Joe Price, Modella’s managing director, said: “When TG Jones was acquired in 2025, it was a loss-making business with an uncertain future. Turning it around meant taking some hard decisions, including closing stores through a court-approved restructuring plan.
“We are extremely grateful to our colleagues from across the business for their continued support. The turnaround is starting to deliver, and we are seeing improved trading results,” he added.
TG Jones sale to shake up high street
The auction of TG Jones, first reported by Sky News, will inevitably draw comparisons with the ongoing sale of Poundland, which is racing to avoid collapse after its owners, Gordon Brothers, refused bids which would have kept the discount retailer afloat.
Modella Capital is conscious of the timing, sources close to the process said, though they insisted that TG Jones is in a different position.
The sale of Poundland has centred on a £30m loan Gordon Brothers inherited when it bought the company, which the investment firm has insisted be repaid in full. No such financial instrument would play a part in TG Jones’s auction, it is understood.
Before Modella Capital bought its 480 shops, WH Smith had traded on UK high streets for 233 years, after being established as a newsagent by Henry Walton Smith in 1792.
Modella Capital has garnered a reputation for picking up struggling high street retailers, often putting them into administration soon after buying them.
Claire’s Accessories and The Original Factory Shop both collapsed earlier this year after being bought by the private equity firm, though Hobbycraft, which Modella also owns, has survived its own restructuring plan.
Alex Willson, TG Jones chief executive, said: “As ever, our focus is on providing a great experience for customers, especially with the critical Christmas period coming up.
“We continue to execute our turnaround plan, which is improving our performance month by month. We’re grateful to our fantastic colleagues for their commitment; and to our suppliers, our owner and other stakeholders for their continued support,” he added.

items.title: Ikea UK sales hit £2.26bn as £54m price cuts target cash-strapped shoppers
items.summary: Ikea UK sales rose 0.5 per cent to £2.26bn in its latest financial year, as it invested £54m in lowering prices to attract cash-strapped shoppers. The company reported a strong start to FY26, with sales climbing 4.7 per cent in the first four months, helped by its growing store estate. Yet trading slowed in the...
items.body:
Ikea UK sales rose 0.5 per cent to £2.26bn in its latest financial year, as it invested £54m in lowering prices to attract cash-strapped shoppers.
The company reported a strong start to FY26, with sales climbing 4.7 per cent in the first four months, helped by its growing store estate. Yet trading slowed in the second half as weak consumer confidence and pressure on household budgets weighed on spending.
Ikea invested £54m in August to cut prices across 425 products by an average of 20 per cent, including its Billy bookcase, Hemnes daybed and Poäng armchair.
It has also introduced more than 1,000 seasonal in-store offers between September and December to cash in on the Christmas trading period.
Ikea UK and Ireland chief executive David McCabe said: “I’m incredibly proud that in extremely challenging market conditions, we’ve managed to close financial year 2026 in growth.”
He added: “In September, we started financial year 2027 with a clear priority: to continue giving customers the best possible value for money at a time when every pound matters.”
The retailer’s store expansion helped boost footfall by seven per cent across its 31 UK stores, following openings in Oxford Street, Brighton, Norwich and York towards the end of the previous financial year.
Ikea also opened a smaller-format store in Chester and a Plan and Order Point in Dundee during FY26, followed by another in Aberdeen in October.
Meanwhile, online and remote sales edged up 0.7 per cent, accounting for 43.3 per cent of total home furnishing sales.
Kitchens proved a bright spot, with sales jumping 14 per cent following improvements to its planning and installation services, shorter appointment waiting times and promotional offers.
Ikea also invested £31.5m in its distribution centres in Peterborough and Doncaster to improve fulfilment efficiency, with an expansion at the latter creating 80 jobs.
Looking ahead, Ikea said it would focus on storage and organisation products as more households look to make better use of their existing homes rather than move or renovate.
However, McCabe warned that high business rates continued to hold back investment in the UK.
“The UK has the highest business rates burden of any IKEA market in Europe and the third highest globally,” he said.
“While the Budget avoided adding further costs, it missed an opportunity to back retailers under real pressure, stopping short of addressing the structural challenges holding the sector back.”
